node.label: Mary P. Ryan
node.date_label: Cradle of the Middle Class (1981) · Women in Public (1990) · Civic Wars (1997)
node.description: A historian of gender and American public life whose research follows women’s access to politics beyond formal suffrage. Nancy Fraser’s substantive reading uses Ryan’s evidence of associations, street protest and public participation to question the identification of public life with one bourgeois arena.

proposed_edges.relationship: Documents women’s public political activity through associations, protests and street participation despite exclusion from suffrage.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Fraser61explicitly attributes these historical findings to Ryan; different classes/ethnicities use different routes, not one universal female experience.

proposed_edges.relationship: Provides historical evidence against equating public politics with a single bourgeois public sphere.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Fraser61uses Ryan’s findings to critique Habermas; this is Fraser’s mediated deployment of Ryan, not evidence Ryan adopted every element of Fraser’s theory or belonged to the Frankfurt School.
